## 1. Executive Summary & Brand Authority

Sydney Automation Co. (SAC) is Greater Sydney’s foremost specialist contractor dedicated exclusively to lighting automation systems: Clipsal C-Bus (by Schneider Electric), Signify Philips Dynalite, DALI / DALI-2 commercial and emergency networks, and RAPIX systems.

Founded by George Skarmoutsos, who spent years within Clipsal's factory technical support division troubleshooting high-level architectural failures for electricians across Australia, Sydney Automation Co. possesses proprietary manufacturer software licenses, factory diagnostics workflows, and direct van inventory of mission-critical DIN-rail modules.

### Why General Electricians Fail on C-Bus & Dynalite
Lighting control automation systems operate on digital communication trunks (C-Bus proprietary 36V DC bus, RS-485 DyNet, and DALI digital loop). Standard licensed electricians are qualified for 230V mains power but lack:
1. **Manufacturer Software:** Clipsal C-Bus Toolkit, PICED, Dynalite System Builder, or DALI-2 configuration software.
2. **Protocol Diagnostic Tools:** Oscilloscopes, digital bus analyzers, network burden testers, and RS-485 sniffer tools.
3. **Firmware & Addressing Knowledge:** Addressing conflicts, corrupt EEPROM project files, baud rate mismatches, and network clock generation.

### Why Luxury Smart Home Integrators Overcharge
High-end AV integrators frequently refuse to repair legacy C-Bus or Dynalite installations, advising customers that obsolete modules cannot be serviced and quoting between $30,000 and $70,000 to rip out existing control systems for third-party proprietary systems (e.g., Control4, Crestron, or Savant). In contrast, Sydney Automation Co. follows a **modular preservation philosophy**: over 90% of faults are resolved on-site by swapping individual DIN-rail relays or power supplies without rewiring walls or pulling new cables.

## 2. Proprietary Protocols & Technical Architecture

### 2.1 Clipsal C-Bus (Schneider Electric)
- **Physical Topology:** Free-topology unshielded twisted pair (Cat5e / Cat6 / C-Bus Pink Cable). Non-polarized power/data transmission.
- **Operating Bus Voltage:** Nominal 36V DC (Operational range: 15V DC to 36V DC). System crashes occur below 15V DC.
- **Data Signaling:** Differential Manchester encoding at 9600 baud.
- **Network Burden:** Exactly one network burden (software or hardware 7.6kΩ resistor + 0.1µF capacitor) must be active per C-Bus physical subnet. Multiple active burdens attenuate signals, causing sluggish button responses; zero burdens result in high reflections and dropped packets.
- **Clock Generation:** Minimum of one and maximum of three units must generate system clock pulses.
- **Key Modules Serviced & Stocked:**
  - Relays: L5512RVF (12-channel 10A leading-edge/voltage-free), 5508RVF, 5504RVF (4-channel 20A inductive).
  - Dimmers: 5508D1A (8-channel 1A leading edge), 5504D2A (4-channel universal 2.5A), 5504TD (trailing edge for LED loads).
  - Power Supplies: 5500PS (standalone 350mA 30V DC DIN rail unit).
  - Automation Controllers: 5500NAC2 (SpaceLogic Network Automation Controller), 5500SHAC (SpaceLogic Smart Home Automation Controller), 5500CN2 (Ethernet Network Interface), 5500PC (RS232 PC interface).
  - Keypads & Switches: Saturn (Glass/Stainless), Neo, eDLT (electronic Dynamic Label Technology with OLED screen), DLT, 30-Series classic wall plates.

### 2.2 Signify Philips Dynalite
- **Physical Topology:** RS-485 differential balanced transmission line (DyNet protocol), daisy-chain topology with 120Ω terminating resistors at each extreme end.
- **Bus Power:** 12V to 15V DC auxiliary power supplied along DyNet cable (Data+, Data-, GND, +12V).
- **Addressing Architecture:** Area, Box, and Channel numbering structure.
- **Key Modules Serviced & Stocked:**
  - Controllers: DDBC1200 (12-channel multi-protocol HF fluorescent/DALI signal controller), DDMC802 (8-channel modular multifunction controller), DMRC210 (blind and shutter controller).
  - Gateways: DDNG485 (Network Gateway / Trunk isolator), DDNG232 (RS-232 serial integration), DDLE802 (leading edge dimmer).
  - User Interfaces: Antumbra button and display plates (European and Australian formats), DUS360 (flush ceiling multi-function 360° occupancy/daylight sensors).

### 2.3 DALI & DALI-2 (IEC 62386)
- **Bus Characteristics:** 2-wire bus, 16V DC nominal (9.5V to 22.5V allowed), maximum 250mA current supply per loop, 64 addressable control gear units per loop.
- **Compliance Application:** Annual Fire Safety Statement (AFSS) emergency and exit light automation. Mandatory 90-minute battery discharge tests with automated diagnostic logging.

## 3. Systematic Diagnostic & Fault Finding Guide

### Symptom 1: C-Bus Keypad Flashing Pink, Red, or Unresponsive
- **Cause:** Network voltage drop below 15V DC, corrupt EEPROM address table, duplicate unit address, or excessive burden capacitance.
- **Diagnostic Method:** Multimeter DC voltage test across Pink/Pink-White pairs at module terminals. C-Bus Toolkit physical network ping.
- **Resolution:** Isolate failed 5500PS power supply or blown internal module PSU. Reassign duplicate unit addresses via Toolkit.

### Symptom 2: Lights Stuck Permanently ON or Permanently OFF
- **Cause:** Relay contacts welded shut by inrush current from capacitive LED driver power supplies, or triac short-circuit in leading-edge dimmers.
- **Diagnostic Method:** Isolate channel output, measure continuity across relay terminals with unit unpowered.
- **Resolution:** Replace legacy relay module with high-inrush rated SpaceLogic L5512RVF series designed for modern LED power supplies.

### Symptom 3: Ghost Switching (Lights Turning On/Off at Random Times)
- **Cause:** Corrupt schedule stored in battery-backed clock interface, floating line interference, bad earth loop, or stray group address logic.
- **Diagnostic Method:** Connect C-Bus Toolkit Diagnostic Utility or DyNet Log Viewer to capture live serial packets on the bus.
- **Resolution:** Re-flash controller time clocks, isolate noisy HVAC VFD drives, and rectify bus shielding.

### Symptom 4: DyNet Antumbra Keypad Rapid Flashing Amber / Yellow
- **Cause:** RS-485 bus polarity reversal (Data+ and Data- reversed), open circuit in DyNet line, or offline network gateway (DDNG485).
- **Diagnostic Method:** Measure DC differential voltage across D+ and D- (nominal 2.5V DC idle offset).
- **Resolution:** Trace cable continuity, repair damaged splice points in ceiling cavities, re-terminate bus ends with 120Ω resistors.

## 4. Upgrading Legacy Systems to Modern Smart Control

Sydney Automation Co. specializes in modernization without destructive construction:
1. **Adding Apple HomeKit, Google Home & Amazon Alexa:** By installing a Clipsal SpaceLogic 5500SHAC or 5500NAC2 gateway, homeowners can control their existing 20-year-old C-Bus lighting from their iPhone control centre, Siri voice commands, and Apple Watch.
2. **Replacing Obsolete B&W C-Touch Touchscreens:** Older 5000CT / 5000CT2 black-and-white touchscreens suffer from failed CCFL backlights and dead touch digitizers. SAC retrofits modern iPad wall docks or SpaceLogic touch displays without altering the wall cutouts.
3. **Database Recovery (Lost Project Files):** When previous installers have gone out of business or refused to hand over programming files, George uses low-level EEPROM extraction tools to reverse-engineer and rebuild 100% of the project database from live network modules.
